section_summary.extract_value: This section reports that body appreciation was significantly lower among sexual minority men (M = 3.29, SE = .06) than heterosexual men (M = 3.55, SE = .04), t(177282) = 3.22, p = .001, with a moderate effect size (Cohen's d = 0.36). The authors conducted mediation analyses (10,000 bootstrapped samples using PROCESS) testing perceived appearance pressures (media only), appearance-ideal internalisation (general and athletic), and upward appearance-based social comparisons; athletic internalisation partially mediated the relationship, while social comparisons fully mediated it, and indirect effects for media pressures and general internalisation were reported in Table 3. The section notes a subsample of sexual minority men (and mentions participants who indicated "rather not say" (n = 7) or did not answer (n = 1)), and refers readers to Table 3 for detailed results.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences: "As hypothesised, levels of body appreciation were significantly lower among sexual minority men (M = 3.29, SE = .06) compared to heterosexual men (M = 3.55, SE = .04), t(177282) = 3.22, p = .001. The magnitude of this difference was moderate, Cohen's d = 0.36 (Cohen, 1992)." and "To do so, we conducted bootstrapping analyses with 10,000 bootstrapped samples using the Version 3 PROCESS macro (Hayes, 2017)." and "The results of these analyses are presented in Table 3... the relationship between sexual orientation and body appreciation was partially mediated by athletic appearance-ideal internalisation... fully mediated by social comparisons." Also: "Total α may differ... participants who indicated their sexual orientation as 'rather not say' (α = 7) or did not answer the question (α = 1) were not categorised as heterosexual or sexual minority."
